decisions.reason: The same message separately changes the Small Block draw condition to approximately every 500 primary-mint or secondary sales, and that change is already represented by its existing message-143 MODIFY.
The FAQ Requirement already records from message 143 that both prize blocks are triggered by mint and secondary sales; no additional change is required.
Making secondary sales eligible for the Big Block draw trigger does not change the royalty amount, visibility, enforcement, founder share, or existing prize-pool destinations.
The candidate already records that primary-mint revenue funds both prize pools, while the source change concerns which sales count toward the Big Block draw trigger rather than revenue allocation.
Changing eligible sale types for the Big Block trigger does not alter the candidate's ticket-based eligibility, Chainlink VRF randomness, or on-chain winner-selection method.
Secondary sales counting toward a prize-block draw does not mean they generate referral tickets; the existing ticket issuance and reset rules remain unchanged.
The eligible sales that trigger a Big Block draw do not change the manual one-click prize claim flow or its Winners-page location.
The source decision governs sales counted toward the Big Block draw trigger and does not change reward allocation when a primary mint has no referral code.
The Big Block trigger's eligible sale types do not change the Transak provider, supported fiat payment methods, conversion behavior, or wallet requirement.
The source decision does not change which ticket counters, badges, or referral-code attributes must appear in NFT metadata.
Counting primary mints and secondary sales toward the Big Block draw does not alter the book, referral code, badges, or expired-ticket state transferred on NFT resale.
The source change to Big Block trigger eligibility does not alter badge designs, referral milestones, storage, or current badge effects.
